content:
Apple has filed for an injunction in its ongoing trade secrets lawsuit against OpenAI. Apple says it will suffer "irreparable harm" from the alleged misappropriation of trade secrets if the court doesn't grant a preliminary injunction.

In its filing, Apple said that after filing its initial lawsuit last month, it reached out to OpenAI and expressed its "intent to seek preliminary injunctive relief." However, Apple said OpenAI could avoid that step if it agreed to five conditions:

  • Stop accessing or using Apple's confidential information
  • Stop any ongoing use or disclosure
  • Preserve all evidence
  • Allow forensic inspection of devices, cloud storage, email, Slack, Teams, and other databases
  • Search OpenAI's systems for any of Apple's confidential information

According to Apple, OpenAI agreed to the first three conditions, but the two sides couldn't agree on the last two.

So Apple is now asking the court to issue a preliminary injunction that would immediately bar OpenAI from using or accessing any Apple trade secrets, preserve all evidence, allow Apple to conduct forensic inspections of OpenAI's devices and accounts, and return any Apple confidential information still in OpenAI's possession.

Apple also filed a separate motion asking the court to speed up discovery, including earlier document production requests and out-of-court depositions of OpenAI's key employees and management.

Beyond these legal filings, OpenAI has now also issued its most comprehensive public response to Apple's lawsuit. In a late-night blog post, OpenAI described the "sloppy, combative, inexplicably targeted lawsuit" as beneath the reputation of "one of the greatest companies in history."

The injunction hearing is scheduled for October 1, 2026. The full filing is available below.
